subject: Order form commercial clarifications: entity split, pricing ladder, tax evidence
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: ClearDepth order form draft – invoices & entity mapping

Kim — attaching the latest Order Form (v3) that Legal and I worked through with Sales Ops. Marianne from ClearDepth asked for a couple of items we should confirm before sending the official redline: 

- ClearDepth wants the invoice to be split between ClearDepth, Inc. (US) and ClearDepth EU AB (Ireland). They also asked for a single signed Order Form covering both entities.
- Procurement asked for a tax-evidence packet (W-9 for US entity; W-8BEN-E or Irish VAT cert for EU).
- Net terms request: they asked for Net45 but also flagged potential preference for Net60 on pilot usage.
- Minimum commit: the draft includes a 12-month mincommit with a stair-step pricing ladder — they want clarity on how usage is allocated across entities for commit credit.

Can you review the attached and advise on (a) whether we can accept the two-entity invoicing approach with a single Order Form, (b) if Net45 is acceptable or if we should push back to Net30/Net45 compromise, and (c) what evidence we need to provide for tax?

Attachment: OrderForm_draft_v3.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — if easier we can jump on a quick 15 min call.

— Ben
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Marianne Cross <marianne.cross@cleardepth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ClearDepth order form draft – invoices & entity mapping

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the draft. A few clarifications from Procurement so we can push this through Finance: 

1) Invoice split: we will pay from two legal entities. ClearDepth, Inc. (US) should be invoiced for US-hosted usage and the EU entity for Europe usage. Can Redwood produce separate invoices tied to those legal entities while keeping a single Order Form and SOW? Procurement prefers a single commercial agreement but separate remit-to details per invoice.

2) Tax evidence: we will need W-9 for ClearDepth, Inc. and either an Irish VAT registration certificate or a valid W-8BEN-E for ClearDepth EU AB. Please include a short cover note describing what tax documents you will provide and which entity they apply to.

3) Net terms: we generally target Net45. For pilots we can agree on Net60 for the first 60 days if Redwood needs the runway, but final terms should be Net45 thereafter.

4) Minimum commit: the customer wants the commit to be applied at the consolidated account level (so usage by either entity counts against the total minimum commit). If you cannot allow consolidated commit crediting, they'll need to carve out separate commit lines which will affect pricing.

Please send back a redline and an attachments list; procurement will route to Accounting and Legal.

Regards,
Marianne Cross
Director, Procurement | ClearDepth
marianne.cross@cleardepth.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marianne Cross <marianne.cross@cleardepth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ClearDepth order form draft – invoices & entity mapping

Marianne — thanks for the clear ask. Quick internal note below and attached a short commercials redline for your review. High-level proposals: 

- Single Order Form: accept (we can keep a single Order Form that references two remit-to invoice entities). We will issue separate invoices by entity per your remit instructions.
- Commit application: propose consolidated commit crediting across both entities. Operationally we will track usage per entity and apply credit against the consolidated commit (this preserves the customer pricing ladder). If Finance needs separate legal entities for revenue recognition we will provide a mapping in the invoices and in monthly reporting.
- Net terms: propose Net45 standard; allow Net60 for the pilot tranche only (first invoice cycle). We'll include language to revert to Net45 post-pilot.
- Tax evidence: we can provide W-9 for Redwood's records? (note: Redwood requires their W-9 on file for the US entity). However, for ClearDepth we will need the tax docs from the customer — we can bundle what Redwood will provide (invoice detail template, tax residency declarations, and any tax withholding statements) and list the docs we require from ClearDepth.

I've attached the commercials_redline_20261114.xlsx with proposed edits (pricing ladder table, commit allocation clause, invoice remit block, and sample invoice line items to ensure accounting can map revenue).

If those points sound ok I'll get Legal to add the specific clause language (Order Form section 2.1: "Invoice Entity and Remittance; Consolidated Commit") and Finance to confirm invoice footer language for EU VAT handling.

Attachment: commercials_redline_20261114.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marianne Cross <marianne.cross@cleardepth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: ClearDepth order form draft – invoices & entity mapping

Kim / Jonas — thanks for the quick turn. I agree with Kimberly's practical approach (single Order Form, separate invoices by remit entity, consolidated commit crediting). A few operational points for visibility before Legal and Finance sign off: 

- Billing ops: we'll need a remit-id field on each invoice (entity tax id + remit address) so the customer's AR team can route. I'll work with Billing to add that to the invoice template.
- Revenue recognition: Jonas, can you confirm if consolidated commit crediting will cause any material change to revenue deferral mechanics (we may need to route some revenue to the EU entity if legal title requires). If so we'll communicate up-front.
- Taxes & withholding: Marianne, once ClearDepth provides the W-9 and the EU VAT cert (or W-8BEN-E), Billing will include a tax evidence package with the first invoice for each entity. For EU VAT treatment we will add the invoice-level VAT breakdown per your guidelines.

Next steps: Legal will draft the final language (Order Form section 2.1 + invoice remit exhibit). Finance to confirm revenue recognition note by EOD Friday. I'll assemble the combined packet (redlined Order Form + sample invoices + checklist) and drop it into the HubSpot deal record.

Thanks — looping Laura for Revenue Ops review.

— Ben
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
